 'It's like Paris Hilton giving a history lesson': Girly Pop Tours to go after agents' solo and LGBTQ+ travellers with 'scandalous' walking tours 
 Operators 
 Dea Jusufi
 17 November 2026
 Girly Pop Tours is looking to grow its trade business with the launch of its second adults-only tour, which combines historical storytelling with a healthy dose of "scandal" and is aimed at solo female and LGBTQ+ travellers.
 Girlypop Tours 
 The 'gossip-style' walking tours, launched in Rome last year, have just recently expanded to Dublin
 Founded by Chloe Schmid, the business debuted its first experience in Rome last year with its second, in Dublin, going live on Tuesday (17 November).
 Tours of London and Paris are planned for early 2027, with Florence, Venice and Barcelona on Girly Pop's longer-term roadmap.
 The concept was born of Schmid's own experiences as a solo traveller and her frustration with conventional sightseeing tours while working in Italy.
 "I was just so bored," she said. "I was walking around these beautiful sights but listening to a boring Wikipedia page."
 Schmid, who studied History and Classics at University College Galway, wanted to find a different way to bring history to life, particularly for Gen Z and millennial travellers.
 Girlypop Tours 
 The tours focus on the scandals, rivalries and romantic entanglements behind historical figures, before ending with a glittery Guinness – or aperol, depending on the area
 "The idea of presenting history like it's gossip was really to make history palatable for younger people who might not necessarily have any previous interest," she said.
 Describing the format as "Paris Hilton giving you a history lesson", the tours focus on the scandals, rivalries and romantic entanglements behind historical figures.
 The new Dublin experience, for example, explores the connections between Irish literary figures like Bram Stoker, Oscar Wilde and Jonathan Swift, including the rivalry between Stoker and Wilde after the former became involved with Wilde's fiancee.
 "These people did amazing things, but they were messy behind the scenes," Schmid said.
 The social aspect is just as important as the storytelling, Schmid said, explaining she wanted to create an experience where solo travellers could "really be themselves, ask the stupid questions, be silly and have fun".
 The Dublin tour runs from Trinity College to Temple Bar, finishing with a glittery Guinness. In Rome, it's a glittery Aperol spritz.
 'I'm targeting a 30-40% trade split'
 Most customers currently book as solo travellers, although the business can accommodate private groups of up to 30 people, including hen parties, friends' trips and corporate bookings.
 For travel agents, private tours are a key part of the proposition, according to Schmid. Groups of four or more can book an exclusive experience from €85 per person in Rome and €95 in Dublin. Public tours are priced at €70 in Rome and €80 in Dublin, with typical bookings comprising five to seven guests.
 Girly Pop Tours offers agent partners a baseline commission of 10%, with trade rates, marketing materials and direct support also available. Schmid said commission arrangements could be negotiated depending on the business generated, while private fam trips can be arranged on request.
 Girlypop Tours 
 Groups of four or more can book an 'exclusive experience' from €85 per person in Rome and €95 in Dublin, while public tours are priced at €70 and €80 respectively
 The operator is currently generating most bookings directly, but hopes to grow the trade channel to account for 30-40% of business within the next year.
 Schmid develops the tour scripts herself, with experiences delivered by freelance local hosts in each destination. She said maintaining a "consistent storytelling format" would be important as the business expands, although she is currently prioritising "quality over quantity".
 "I'd rather make sure what we're doing in each city is well received and we're getting really good feedback, rather than growing too quickly and then the quality decreases," she said.
 The Dublin tour offers departures from Thursday to Sunday at 2.00pm. Rome tours run daily, with a 3.30pm winter departure.
